primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Ménétrier disease due to excessive TGF-alpha/EGFR signaling
mechanism: Ménétrier disease is an acquired hypertrophic gastropathy driven by excessive transforming growth factor alpha signaling through the epidermal growth factor receptor. This causes marked foveolar epithelial hyperplasia, glandular atrophy with reduced parietal-cell mass and acid secretion, enlarged proximal gastric rugal folds, and protein loss across abnormal gastric mucosa, producing hypoalbuminemia and edema.
vignette: A 55-year-old man has several months of epigastric discomfort, early satiety, fatigue, and progressive ankle edema. Laboratory studies show hypoalbuminemia without proteinuria or evidence of chronic liver disease. Upper endoscopy demonstrates markedly enlarged rugal folds involving the gastric body and fundus with relative sparing of the antrum. Gastric biopsy shows prominent foveolar hyperplasia and glandular atrophy.
lead: Which of the following molecular changes most directly contributes to this patient's gastric disorder?
correct: Increased transforming growth factor alpha activation of epidermal growth factor receptors in gastric mucosal epithelium
distractors: Autonomous gastrin secretion causing sustained stimulation of parietal-cell acid production
Loss of APC function causing constitutive beta-catenin signaling in gastric epithelial stem cells
Autoantibody-mediated destruction of parietal cells with secondary hypergastrinemia
T-cell-mediated injury triggered by gluten-derived peptides presented by HLA-DQ2 or HLA-DQ8
distractor_notes: Autonomous gastrin secretion describes Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, which causes acid hypersecretion and peptic disease rather than the protein-losing foveolar hypertrophy in this vignette.
APC loss and beta-catenin activation are central to conventional colorectal adenoma-carcinoma tumorigenesis, not Ménétrier disease.

Autoimmune gastritis destroys parietal cells and can produce achlorhydria and hypergastrinemia, but it causes atrophic gastritis rather than giant proximal folds with foveolar hyperplasia and protein loss.
HLA-DQ2/DQ8-mediated gluten sensitivity describes celiac disease, a small-intestinal enteropathy rather than hypertrophic gastric mucosal disease.
key_expl: The combination of giant proximal gastric folds, foveolar hyperplasia, glandular atrophy, hypoalbuminemia, and edema is classic for Ménétrier disease. Excess TGF-alpha activates EGFR in gastric mucosal epithelium, promoting foveolar proliferation and mucus production while contributing to glandular atrophy and reduced acid secretion. Abnormal mucosal permeability and mucus-rich protein loss cause protein-losing gastropathy.
objective: Recognize Ménétrier disease and link its giant gastric folds, foveolar hyperplasia, hypochlorhydria, and protein loss to excessive TGF-alpha/EGFR signaling.
clues: giant gastric folds in body and fundus
hypoalbuminemia with edema and no renal/hepatic cause
